# atlas-config

Minimal config for the agents Ed uses, managed with [GNU Stow](https://www.gnu.org/software/stow/) and [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just).

This repo intentionally starts small. Items are cherry-picked and added over time as needed — no pre-built skill/hook bundles, no auto-loaded frameworks. If it's here, it's because it earned its keep.

## Layout

| Package      | Source                  | Stowed to        |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------- |
| `claudecode` | `claudecode/.claude/`   | `~/.claude/`     |
| `pi`         | `pi/.pi/agent/`         | `~/.pi/agent/`   |
| `codex`      | `codex/.codex/`         | `~/.codex/`      |

Plans, handoffs, and worktrees live under `.atlas/` at the repo root (see `.atlas/plans/`, `.atlas/handoffs/`).

## Commands

```bash
just link     # first-time setup — create symlinks for all packages
just up       # restow after adding/removing files (alias: just update)
just unlink   # remove all symlinks
just status   # dry run — show what stow would do
just push     # commit any changes and push to origin
```

## Notes

- `pi/` is a placeholder while the Pi agent is reconfigured. Add files there as needed and `just up` to stow them.
- `oldSetup/`, `.audit-backup/`, and any `auth.json` files are gitignored — runtime state and local backups never get committed.
- Codex runtime state stays local; only curated files like `config.toml` and `hooks.json` are stowed.
- Worktrees (`EnterWorktree` / `ExitWorktree`) write to `.atlas/worktrees/`, which is also gitignored.

# atlas-config — Agent Instructions

This repo is a minimal, stow-managed config for Ed's agents. The previous Atlas/PAI build (skills, hooks, VoiceServer, Observability, multi-agent coordination) was removed on 2026-05-01 — the goal now is to cherry-pick configuration as needs arise rather than ship a pre-built framework.

## Repo layout

| Package      | Source                  | Stowed to        | Status                                           |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `claudecode` | `claudecode/.claude/`   | `~/.claude/`     | Empty — Claude Code itself was freshly installed |
| `pi`         | `pi/.pi/agent/`         | `~/.pi/agent/`   | Placeholder — Pi will be reconfigured over time  |

Project-local artifacts live under `.atlas/` (`plans/`, `handoffs/`, `worktrees/`). `worktrees/` is gitignored.

## Stow

Multi-package stow with the repo root as `STOW_DIR`. See `justfile` for commands. The per-package `.stow-local-ignore` files **replace** stow's built-in defaults — when adding a new one, copy from `claudecode/.stow-local-ignore` and re-include `\.git`, `\.gitignore`, etc.

## When adding files

- Adding to `claudecode/.claude/` or `pi/.pi/agent/` → run `just up` to restow.
- Anything that should not be symlinked into the runtime location → add a pattern to that package's `.stow-local-ignore`.
- Secrets (`auth.json`, `*.env`, keys) → already covered by `.gitignore`. Do not weaken those rules.

## Notable conventions

- `.atlas/plans/` for active plan/design docs, `.atlas/plans/archive/` for completed.
- `.atlas/handoffs/` for live handoffs, archived to `.atlas/handoffs/archive/` when consumed.
- File naming: `YYYY-MM-DD-description.md`.
- Use git worktrees (`EnterWorktree` / `ExitWorktree`) for implementation work — they land in `.atlas/worktrees/`.

repo=edheltzel/atlas-config
tmp=$(mktemp -d)

cat > "$tmp/01-global-flow-command.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem
Atlas Pi config should stay minimal globally, but projects need a discoverable way to install Pi extensions, skills, and templates on demand for specific work modes. Today there is no curated global slash command that can bootstrap a project flow without preloading a broad framework everywhere.

## Proposed command UX
Add one global Pi slash command, tentatively `/atlas-flow`, stowed from `pi/.pi/agent/`, with subcommands:

- `/atlas-flow list` — show available flows and what each installs.
- `/atlas-flow preview <flow>` — dry-run global extensions and project-local files to be installed.
- `/atlas-flow install <flow> [--project .] [--yes]` — install only the selected flow.
- `/atlas-flow remove <flow> [--project .]` — remove project-local artifacts created by the flow where safe.
- `/atlas-flow status` — report installed Atlas flow metadata for the current project.

The command should prefer project-local skills/templates and install global Pi extensions only when a flow explicitly requires them.

## Flow package contents
- **Global extensions:** only the slash command itself and a tiny flow installer/registry. Optional extensions are installed lazily per flow.
- **Project-local skills/templates:** flow manifests, prompts, README snippets, checklists, and generated `.pi` project artifacts created inside the target project.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single global slash command is available after stowing Pi config.
- The command can list, preview, install, remove, and report status for flow packages.
- Flow manifests distinguish required global Pi extensions from project-local skills/templates.
- Installation is idempotent and records metadata in the target project.
- Dry-run output clearly identifies global changes vs project-local changes.
- Documentation explains why flows are on-demand rather than globally preinstalled.

## Notes about keeping global install surface minimal
Do not recreate the old Atlas/PAI framework as an always-loaded bundle. Keep global config to the command/installer and perhaps a small manifest. Everything else should be installed only when a user selects a flow.
EOF

cat > "$tmp/02-marketing-flow.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem
Marketing work often needs repeatable agent support for SEO, social media, blogging/content operations, and analytics, but these capabilities should not be globally loaded for every coding project.

## Proposed command UX
- `/atlas-flow preview marketing`
- `/atlas-flow install marketing [--project .]`
- `/atlas-flow status`

Installer output should show which marketing skills/templates are added and any optional extensions needed for web/content workflows.

## Flow package contents
- **Global extensions:** none by default unless the installer needs an approved Pi extension for project-local skill registration. Optional web/search integrations should be explicit and user-confirmed.
- **Project-local skills/templates:**
  - SEO audit and keyword brief skill.
  - Content calendar/blog operations skill.
  - Social post repurposing templates for LinkedIn/X/newsletter snippets.
  - Analytics review checklist for GA/Search Console/exported CSVs.
  - Content brief, editorial QA, and publish checklist templates.

## Acceptance criteria
- Installing the marketing flow creates project-local marketing skills/templates only in the target project.
- Preview identifies SEO, social, blog/content ops, and analytics components.
- Skills include prompts/checklists for content audits, briefs, calendars, and channel repurposing.
- No global marketing-specific tools are installed unless explicitly confirmed.

## Notes about keeping global install surface minimal
Marketing assets are project-specific and should live with the marketing project. The global command should only fetch/apply this package on demand.
EOF

cat > "$tmp/03-ssg-ssr-flow.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem
SSG/SSR website projects need agent support for framework-aware workflows, performance, accessibility, routing, content, and deployment checks. These should be available on demand without expanding the global Pi baseline.

## Proposed command UX
- `/atlas-flow preview web-ssg-ssr`
- `/atlas-flow install web-ssg-ssr [--project .] [--framework next|astro|nuxt|sveltekit|auto]`

The command should detect common frameworks where possible and select templates accordingly.

## Flow package contents
- **Global extensions:** none by default; optional browser/test tooling extensions only if Pi requires them and the user confirms.
- **Project-local skills/templates:**
  - Framework detection and project map template.
  - SSG/SSR routing/data-fetching review skill.
  - Performance/Core Web Vitals checklist.
  - Accessibility and semantic HTML review checklist.
  - SEO metadata/sitemap/robots checklist.
  - Deployment/runtime environment checklist.

## Acceptance criteria
- Installer supports an auto-detect path and a manual framework override.
- Flow includes templates for at least Next.js, Astro, Nuxt, and SvelteKit or a documented fallback for unknown frameworks.
- Generated project-local assets guide build/test/lint/performance checks without hardcoding one framework globally.
- Preview separates optional browser/test extensions from local templates.

## Notes about keeping global install surface minimal
Framework-specific guidance should be installed per website project. Avoid global SSG/SSR hooks or background behavior.
EOF

cat > "$tmp/04-video-flow.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem
Video creation/editing workflows need structured support for scripting, shot lists, edit planning, metadata, and publishing, but those assets are irrelevant to most engineering repos.

## Proposed command UX
- `/atlas-flow preview video`
- `/atlas-flow install video [--project .]`

The command should present optional packages for short-form, long-form, tutorial, or course-style video projects.

## Flow package contents
- **Global extensions:** none by default. Optional media/transcription integrations should be separately confirmed if available.
- **Project-local skills/templates:**
  - Video concept brief and audience/outcome template.
  - Script, outline, and storyboard skills.
  - Shot list and b-roll checklist.
  - Editing review checklist for pacing, audio, captions, and visual continuity.
  - Publishing metadata templates for YouTube, Shorts/Reels/TikTok, thumbnails, and descriptions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Installing the flow creates local video planning/editing/publishing assets.
- Templates cover scripting, production, editing QA, and publishing metadata.
- Optional transcription/media extensions are not installed silently.
- Flow can be used in non-code content project directories.

## Notes about keeping global install surface minimal
Video skills/templates should be local to video projects. Keep the global command content-agnostic.
EOF

cat > "$tmp/05-ui-ux-consulting-flow.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem
UI/UX consulting projects need repeatable discovery, heuristic review, research synthesis, design critique, and handoff workflows. These are valuable but too specialized for global Pi config.

## Proposed command UX
- `/atlas-flow preview ui-ux-consulting`
- `/atlas-flow install ui-ux-consulting [--project .]`

The command should install consulting deliverable templates and review skills into a client/project workspace.

## Flow package contents
- **Global extensions:** none by default; optional screenshot/browser integrations only with confirmation.
- **Project-local skills/templates:**
  - Client intake and goals/constraints template.
  - UX heuristic evaluation skill.
  - IA/navigation and user journey mapping templates.
  - Accessibility review checklist.
  - Design critique and annotated findings template.
  - Prioritized recommendations and executive summary template.

## Acceptance criteria
- Flow installs project-local consulting templates suitable for client engagements.
- Deliverables include intake, heuristic review, findings, recommendations, and executive summary.
- Preview identifies optional visual/browser tooling separately from local artifacts.
- No UI/UX-specific global hooks or skills are loaded by default.

## Notes about keeping global install surface minimal
Consulting deliverables belong in the client project. Global config should only expose the on-demand installer.
EOF

cat > "$tmp/06-infra-ipsec-pentest-flow.md" <<'EOF'
## Problem
Infra, IPsec, and pentesting consulting work needs careful scoping, evidence capture, remediation tracking, and security-specific checklists. It must be opt-in and project-scoped to avoid loading sensitive/security tooling globally.

## Proposed command UX
- `/atlas-flow preview infra-ipsec-pentest`
- `/atlas-flow install infra-ipsec-pentest [--project .]`

The installer should display safety/legal reminders and require explicit confirmation before installing security workflow assets.

## Flow package contents
- **Global extensions:** none by default. Any network, scanner, or credential-related extension must be optional, documented, and explicitly confirmed.
- **Project-local skills/templates:**
  - Rules of engagement and authorization checklist.
  - Asset/scope inventory template.
  - IPsec/VPN configuration review checklist.
  - Infra hardening checklist.
  - Pentest finding template with severity, evidence, impact, and remediation.
  - Remediation tracker and final report outline.

## Acceptance criteria
- Flow installation requires an explicit safety/authorization acknowledgement.
- Templates emphasize authorized testing, scoping, evidence handling, and remediation.
- No active scanning or credential tooling is installed globally by default.
- Preview clearly separates documentation/checklist assets from any optional security extensions.

## Notes about keeping global install surface minimal
Security and network tooling has a higher risk profile. Keep defaults to local documentation/templates and require deliberate opt-in for anything executable or global.
EOF

for f in "$tmp"/*.md; do
  base=$(basename "$f")
  case "$base" in
    01*) title="Add minimal global /atlas-flow command for on-demand Pi flows" ;;
    02*) title="Add on-demand Marketing flow for SEO, social, content ops, and analytics" ;;
    03*) title="Add on-demand SSG/SSR website flow" ;;
    04*) title="Add on-demand Video creation and editing flow" ;;
    05*) title="Add on-demand UI/UX consulting flow" ;;
    06*) title="Add on-demand Infra, IPsec, and pentesting consulting flow" ;;
  esac
  gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$f"
done
